description: CPU Hartree-Fock through the libcint backend. Reference energies are PySCF RHF on the same geometry and the same basis JSON out of basis_sets/, not values this program produced -- a manifest of its own output would only detect change, not error. Generated by tools/cpu_validation; do not edit by hand. Kept separate from validation_tests.json because that one is xTB and needs tblite, while these need libcint and nothing else. The angular form of each reference follows the basis rather than being assumed: the polarised Pople sets are Cartesian, six d functions rather than five, and computing one as the other is 1.4 mHartree on water under a basis name that means the opposite. Reading the exponents out of basis_sets/ rather than PySCF's own tables matters most for these same sets -- BSE writes them to ten significant figures and PySCF carries more, which alone is worth 1e-7 and looks exactly like a bug in whichever code is checked.
